scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 RIP version
Mechanism: router0 and router1 run RIPv2; router2 was switched
  to RIPv1. The two versions use different packet formats and
  v2 peers drop v1 updates by default (and vice versa). router2
  is "sending" updates that router1 ignores. router2's own
  connected networks stay in its RIB; only advertised ones
  vanish elsewhere.
Localization: router2
Root cause: RIP version mismatch (router2 v1, neighbors v2)
Fix: `vtysh -c "router rip" -c "version 2"` on router2

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a RIP protocol-version mismatch introduced by a configuration
change on router2. router2's RIP daemon was reconfigured with "version 1",
causing it to send RIPv1 broadcasts on all interfaces (including eth2, the
wan_r1_r2 WAN link) and to accept only RIPv1 advertisements in return.
router1, however, is configured with "version 2" globally, meaning it sends
only RIPv2 multicast packets and enforces receive-version 2 on every
interface including eth3 (its end of the same WAN link).

The result is mutual rejection: router1 discards every RIPv1 broadcast
arriving from router2 (confirmed by BadPackets: 3 recorded for gateway
20.20.0.2 in router1's RIP status), and router2 discards every RIPv2
multicast arriving from router1 (BadPackets: 3 for gateway 20.20.0.1 in
router2's RIP status). Because router1 never receives a valid update from
router2, the 180-second RIP timeout is not reset. The routes 1.0.0.0/8 and
128.168.0.0/16 — both directly connected on router2's eth0 and eth1
respectively — are therefore not refreshed on router1 and expire, vanishing
from its routing table. router2 believes it is sending updates (it is), but
router1 silently drops every packet. The remainder of the topology
(router0 ↔ router1) is unaffected because that link is version-consistent.

Root cause: router2's RIP configuration was changed to "version 1" while
router1 remains "version 2", creating an incompatible version pairing on
the wan_r1_r2 segment.

Corrective fix: On router2, enter vtysh, go into "router rip" context, and
replace "version 1" with "version 2" (or remove the version statement to
inherit the FRR default of send-v2/receive-both). This realigns both peers
to RIPv2 and restores bidirectional update exchange on the WAN link.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names router2 as the device with the RIP version misconfiguration.
Clearly identifies an RIP protocol-version mismatch: router2 set to RIPv1 while router1 uses RIPv2.
Correct remediation: update router2's RIP to version 2 (or remove the version line) so it matches router1 and restores updates.
